title: Emergency elevation: just-in-time admin access, attestation and audit-forwarding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a robust, auditable emergency admin elevation mechanism that integrates with RBAC v2, SSO/SAML, and our immutable audit pipeline. This ticket covers the technical design, short-term implementation for oncall break-glass use, and a plan to graduate the flow into a hardened, automated service with full logging and attestation.

Background: We need a safe, time-limited way to grant elevated privileges during incidents without permanently bypassing RBAC or SSO controls. Existing ad-hoc processes (manual password handoffs, privileged accounts) create audit and compliance gaps. The proposed system provides: just-in-time elevation, multi-step attestation, minimal blast radius, and guaranteed audit-forwarding to SIEM.

Requirements (high level):
- Just-in-time temporary elevation that maps to RBAC v2 roles (no permanent role assignment).
- Strong gating: SSO re-auth (SAML assertion), mandatory MFA, and an approval/attestation step for non-trivial elevations.
- Short TTLs (default 15 minutes) with automatic renewal requiring re-attestation.
- Cryptographically-signed elevation tokens recorded to immutable audit log and forwarded to SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle).
- One-click session revoke and emergency kill-switch that immediately revokes active elevated tokens.
- Full audit context: requester, approver(s), justification, trigger (PagerDuty/Slack link), command/session metadata, and system state snapshot.
- Rotation and post-incident key management: keys used to sign tokens must be in KMS/HSM with automated rotation and a clear compromise playbook.

Proposed design (phases):
1) Phase 0 (fast, low-risk) - Engineering prototype for oncall:
   - Implement a scoped elevation service that mints signed short-lived tokens (JWT with KMS key id).
   - Gate issuance with an SSO re-auth check (SAML assertion) and team lead attestation via Slack thread integration or PagerDuty approval.
   - Enforce TTL 15m, single-session token, and store an audit record in the immutable events table.
   - Add a revoke endpoint and a UI modal in Console under "Emergency actions" with timeline.
   - Backfill logs to SIEM via existing audit-forwarder.
2) Phase 1 (harden & integrate) - RBAC v2 binding and automation:
   - Map tokens to RBAC v2 policy bindings; token contains role_id and enforced by runtime (no implicit root).
   - Add MFA enforcement at token request time and require explicit justification fields (structured).
   - Add automatic post-incident workflow to create a curated incident artifact (Confluence page + timeline).
3) Phase 2 (compliance & scale) - Enterprise controls:
   - Attestation chain: signer rotation, HSM-backed keys, and retention/archival policy for tokens and session recordings.
   - Fine-grained audit exports (immutable S3 + SIEM) and e-discovery support.
   - Admin review dashboard and periodic access reports for security/compliance teams.

Non-goals:
- This ticket is not full session recording (video/tty capture) — that will be tracked separately but the design includes hooks for later recording.
- Not replacing privileged service accounts; service account rotation and least-privilege refactors are separate projects.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Approval model: single approver vs quorum. For Phase 0 we default to single approver (oncall lead), Phase 1 moves to quorum for critical scopes.
- Token format: JWT vs opaque token. JWT is easier for debugging and partial validation but opaque tokens with HSM lookup are marginally more secure. We'll start with signed JWTs (KMS) and keep the code paths abstracted for later swap.
- TTL default: 15 minutes (lower blast radius) but some operations may require 1-hour windows; support scoped TTL with mandatory justification.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (Confluence) with sequence diagrams and threat model (linked in comments).
- Phase 0 implementation + Console modal + minimal SIEM forwarding.
- Unit/integration tests and chaos test for revoke path.
- Post-incident runbook template and automation to generate incident artifact.

Acceptance criteria:
- Oncall can request emergency elevation via Console and receive a signed token that permits the elevated RBAC binding.
- Token issuance requires SSO re-auth and an approver attestation.
- Every elevation generates an immutable audit event that appears in SIEM within 5 minutes.
- Revoke endpoint revokes active tokens within 10s under load.
- Security review completed and KMS/HSM keys are provisioned for token signing.
